_notes: Master world palette for Vesperholm tilesets. Every area's tile set derives its --palette from here so the whole world reads as one cohesive place (see docs/world/atlas.md and the generate-sprite-sheet tileset flow). The 8 brand anchors come from src/game/config.ts. The `ramps` give each material a real 4-step value ladder (outline -> dark -> mid -> light) so tiles have proper CONTRAST instead of reading flat and washed-out — the #1 quality lever. Quantise every generated tile to the area's working palette with quantize_to_palette.py. Keep tile sets to ~10-16 flat colours drawn from this set plus the area's 1-2 accents.
_ramp_notes: Each material is a 4-step value ladder: outline (darkest, the deep-ink linework) -> dark (shadow / down-right faces) -> mid (the body colour) -> light (top-left highlight). Use all four on every tile: a tile painted in only its mid colour is the washed-out look we are fixing. The outline step doubles as the area's shared dark so adjacent materials share linework and read as one set.
_autotile_terrains: An autotile terrain is one material rendered as a 47-blob set (corners, edges, inner corners, fill) so a region of it gets clean borders against everything else automatically. Author maps with a `terrain` layer (see docs/world/level-design.md) and expand it with tools/autotile. Typical terrains per area: the ground fill, water, and cliff/ledge. Each terrain pulls its 4-step value ladder from `ramps` above.
